# Load data
```{r load-data-1}
read_ceesat_csv <- function(path) {
  read.csv(path, colClasses = "character", check.names = FALSE,
           na.strings = NULL, strip.white = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
}

transform_ceesat <- function(raw) {
  metadata <- c("study_id", "study_type_title_abstract", "doi", "cited_in_policy")
  questions <- c("1.1", "2.1", "3.1", "3.2", "4.1", "4.2", "4.3",
                 "5.1", "5.2", "6.1", "6.2", "6.3", "7.1", "7.2", "7.3", "8.1")
  if (anyDuplicated(names(raw)) || !all(metadata %in% names(raw))) {
    stop("Dataset4 has duplicate column names or is missing required metadata.")
  }
  if (!nrow(raw) || anyNA(raw$study_id) || any(!nzchar(trimws(raw$study_id))) ||
      anyDuplicated(raw$study_id)) stop("Dataset4 must have unique, nonblank study IDs.")
  if (anyNA(raw$cited_in_policy) ||
      !all(raw$cited_in_policy %in% c("0", "1"))) {
    stop("cited_in_policy must contain only 0 and 1.")
  }
  question_cols <- grep("^[0-9]+[.][0-9]+:", names(raw), value = TRUE)
  question_ids <- sub(":.*$", "", question_cols)
  if (anyDuplicated(question_ids) || !setequal(question_ids, questions)) {
    stop("Dataset4 must contain exactly the 16 expected CEESAT question columns.")
  }
  question_cols <- question_cols[match(questions, question_ids)]
  scores <- c("Red (0)" = 0L, "Amber (1)" = 1L,
              "Green (3)" = 3L, "Gold (4)" = 4L)
  out <- raw[metadata]
  for (i in seq_along(questions)) {
    labels <- trimws(raw[[question_cols[i]]])
    bad <- is.na(labels) | !(labels %in% names(scores))
    if (any(bad)) {
      stop(sprintf("Unknown/missing rating for CEESAT%s: %s", questions[i],
                   paste(raw$study_id[bad], collapse = ", ")))
    }
    out[[paste0("CEESAT", questions[i])]] <- unname(scores[labels])
  }

  # Dataset4's Total Score is blank in the supplied source. Recompute from all
  # 16 items (maximum 64); do not rescale, impute, or use that source total.
  out$raw_score <- rowSums(out[paste0("CEESAT", questions)])
  out
}

validate_ceesat <- function(generated, reference) {
  if (!identical(names(generated), names(reference)) ||
      nrow(generated) != nrow(reference)) {
    stop("Generated and reference datasets have different dimensions or columns.")
  }
  # Check every cell and row order, including metadata and DOI whitespace.
  differences <- lapply(names(reference), function(column) {
    actual <- as.character(generated[[column]])
    expected <- as.character(reference[[column]])
    bad <- which(is.na(actual) != is.na(expected) |
                   (!is.na(actual) & !is.na(expected) & actual != expected))
    if (!length(bad)) return(NULL)
    data.frame(row = bad, study_id = generated$study_id[bad], column = column,
               generated = actual[bad], reference = expected[bad])
  })
  differences <- do.call(rbind, differences)
  if (!is.null(differences)) {
    print(differences, row.names = FALSE)
    stop("Generated values differ from the manual reference; no output was written.")
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Reconstruct in memory and validate every cell against the supplied final Dataset5.
ceesat_generated <- transform_ceesat(read_ceesat_csv(
  here("Data", "Dataset4_ceesat_assessments.csv")))
validate_ceesat(ceesat_generated, read_ceesat_csv(
  here("Data", "Dataset5_ceesat_processed.csv")))

# Load the final datasets after validation; no source files are overwritten.
```

# Main-figure panel-letter style

```{r main-figure-panel-letter-style-1}
# Main-figure lettering is enlarged while retaining the original export dimensions.
# Export main figures at their established dimensions. TIFF/PNG are rendered
# directly at 600 dpi; PDFs use a font-embedding graphics device. No raster upsampling.
export_main_figure <- function(plot, number, stem, width, height,
                               project_root = here::here()) {
  if (!isTRUE(params$export_figures)) return(invisible(NULL))
  final <- file.path(project_root, "Figures", "Final_figures")
  raw <- final
  dir.create(final, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  dir.create(file.path(final, "tiff"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  filename <- paste0("Figure_", number, "_", stem)
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(final, "tiff", paste0("Figure", number, "_", stem, ".tiff")), plot,
    width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = 600,
    device = ragg::agg_tiff, compression = "lzw", bitsize = 8, bg = "white")
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(final, paste0(filename, ".png")), plot,
    width = width, height = height, units = "in", dpi = 600,
    device = ragg::agg_png, bg = "white")
  # Quartz embeds fonts on macOS without requiring a separate XQuartz install.
  pdf_device <- if (identical(Sys.info()[["sysname"]], "Darwin")) {
    function(filename, width, height, bg, ...) {
      grDevices::quartz(type = "pdf", file = filename,
                        width = width, height = height, bg = bg)
    }
  } else grDevices::cairo_pdf
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(raw, paste0(filename, ".pdf")), plot,
    width = width, height = height, units = "in",
    device = pdf_device, bg = "white")
  message("Exported Figure ", number, ": ", width, " x ", height,
          " in; RGB TIFF/PNG 600 dpi and font-embedded PDF.")
  invisible(file.path(final, "tiff", paste0("Figure", number, "_", stem, ".tiff")))
}

# Supplementary figures are exported only on request.
save_supplementary_figure <- function(filename, ...) {
  if (!isTRUE(params$export_figures)) return(invisible(NULL))
  dir.create(dirname(filename), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  ggplot2::ggsave(filename, ...)
}

dir.create(here("Figures", "Final_figures"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

# Figure 1: Systematic-map evidence matrix

## Setup and shared helpers

```{r figure-1-systematic-map-evidence-matrix-1}
figure1_panel_letter <- function() {
  element_text(family = "Helvetica", face = "bold", size = 26, colour = "#243746")
}

n_syntheses <- n_distinct(map$study_id)

# Grey and muted magenta in panel A; panel B retains its original blue-grey gradient.
colours <- c(
  ink = "#243746",
  muted_ink = "#52636F",
  narrative = "#BDBDBD",
  quantitative = "#A34F78",
  marine = "#667A93",
  urban = "#AD8EAF",
  invertebrate = "#53917E",
  freshwater = "#A2BAB6",
  plum = "#8A4A82",
  breadth_multiple = "#243746",
  terrestrial = "#A8A17B",
  slate = "#8A8F98",
  breadth_single = "#DCE7ED",
  pale_tile = "#EDF2F5",
  paper = "white",
  line = "#CBD3D8"
)

split_categories <- function(data, variable) {
  data %>%
    select(study_id, {{ variable }}) %>%
    separate_rows({{ variable }}, sep = ",") %>%
    mutate({{ variable }} := str_trim({{ variable }})) %>%
    filter(!is.na({{ variable }}), {{ variable }} != "") %>%
    distinct()
}

# Label helper: "Transportation (37)".
with_total <- function(label, n) paste0(label, " (", n, ")")


base_size <- 20

theme_map <- function() {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      plot.tag = figure1_panel_letter(),
      plot.tag.position = c(0, 1),
      axis.text = element_text(colour = colours["ink"], size = base_size - 0.5),
      axis.title = element_text(colour = colours["muted_ink"], size = base_size - 1),
      legend.text = element_text(colour = colours["muted_ink"], size = base_size - 1.5),
      legend.title = element_text(colour = colours["muted_ink"], size = base_size - 1.5),
      plot.margin = margin(10, 12, 10, 12)
    )
}
```
## Panel A: Publication year and synthesis approach

```{r figure-1-systematic-map-evidence-matrix-2}
approach_by_year <- map %>%
  transmute(
    study_id,
    year,
    approach = if_else(
      str_to_lower(str_trim(quantitative)) == "yes",
      "Quantitative",
      "Narrative/Descriptive"
    )
  ) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  count(year, approach, name = "n") %>%
  complete(
    year = seq(min(map$year, na.rm = TRUE), max(map$year, na.rm = TRUE)),
    approach = c("Narrative/Descriptive", "Quantitative"),
    fill = list(n = 0)
  )

approach_counts <- approach_by_year %>%
  summarise(n = sum(n), .by = approach)

approach_labels <- set_names(
  with_total(approach_counts$approach, approach_counts$n),
  approach_counts$approach
)

year_totals <- approach_by_year %>%
  summarise(n = sum(n), .by = year) %>%
  filter(n > 0)

panel_a <- ggplot(approach_by_year, aes(x = year, y = n, fill = approach)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62) +
  geom_text(
    data = year_totals,
    aes(x = year, y = n, label = n),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    vjust = -0.6,
    size = base_size / .pt * 0.92,
    colour = colours["muted_ink"]
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Narrative/Descriptive" = unname(colours["narrative"]),
      "Quantitative" = unname(colours["quantitative"])
    ),
    labels = approach_labels,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(min(approach_by_year$year), max(approach_by_year$year), by = 1),
    expand = expansion(mult = 0.015)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = c(0, 5, 10),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.45))
  ) +
  labs(tag = "A", y = "Syntheses", x = NULL) +
  theme_map() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.line.x = element_line(colour = colours["line"], linewidth = 0.3),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 12)),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.key.size = unit(11, "pt")
  )
```
## Panel B: Noise source × biological outcome evidence matrix

```{r figure-1-systematic-map-evidence-matrix-3}
noise_long <- split_categories(map, noise_source)
outcome_long <- split_categories(map, outcome_category)

noise_totals <- noise_long %>%
  count(noise_source, name = "total") %>%
  arrange(desc(total))

outcome_totals <- outcome_long %>%
  count(outcome_category, name = "total") %>%
  arrange(desc(total))

crosstab <- noise_long %>%
  inner_join(outcome_long, by = "study_id", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
  count(noise_source, outcome_category, name = "n") %>%
  complete(
    noise_source = noise_totals$noise_source,
    outcome_category = outcome_totals$outcome_category,
    fill = list(n = 0)
  ) %>%
  left_join(noise_totals, by = "noise_source") %>%
  left_join(outcome_totals, by = "outcome_category") %>%
  mutate(
    noise_label = factor(
      with_total(noise_source, total.x),
      levels = rev(with_total(noise_totals$noise_source, noise_totals$total))
    ),
    outcome_label = factor(
      with_total(outcome_category, total.y),
      levels = with_total(outcome_totals$outcome_category, outcome_totals$total)
    ),
    # White numerals only where the tile is dark enough to carry them.
    label_colour = if_else(n >= 13, "#FFFFFF", unname(colours["ink"]))
  )

panel_b <- ggplot(crosstab, aes(x = outcome_label, y = noise_label, fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(colour = colours["paper"], linewidth = 1.4) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = n, colour = label_colour),
    size = base_size / .pt * 0.95
  ) +
  scale_colour_identity() +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = colours["pale_tile"],
    high = colours["ink"],
    name = "Syntheses per combination",
    guide = guide_colourbar(
      title.position = "top",
      title.vjust = 0.9,
      barwidth = unit(180, "pt"),
      barheight = unit(7, "pt"),
      ticks = FALSE
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top", expand = expansion(0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(0)) +
  labs(tag = "B",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_map() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x.top = element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 0, vjust = 0,
                                   colour = colours["ink"]),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.margin = margin(t = 10)
  )
```
## Panel C: Taxonomic scope

```{r figure-1-systematic-map-evidence-matrix-4}
vertebrate_taxa <- c("Aves", "Mammalia", "Reptilia", "Fish", "Amphibia")
invertebrate_taxa <- c(
  "Invertebrates", "Arthropoda", "Mollusca", "Cnidaria",
  "Echinodermata", "Annelida", "Bryozoa"
)

taxonomic_membership <- map %>%
  select(study_id, scope_taxon) %>%
  separate_rows(scope_taxon, sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(
    scope_taxon = str_to_title(str_trim(scope_taxon)),
    group = case_when(
      scope_taxon %in% vertebrate_taxa ~ "Vertebrate",
      scope_taxon %in% invertebrate_taxa ~ "Invertebrate",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(group)) %>%
  distinct(study_id, group)

# "Mixed" is the overlap of the two groups, not a third exclusive group: those
# syntheses are also counted in the Vertebrate and Invertebrate bars.
taxonomic_overlap <- taxonomic_membership %>%
  count(study_id) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(n == 2)) %>%
  pull(n)

taxonomic_counts <- taxonomic_membership %>%
  count(group, name = "n") %>%
  bind_rows(tibble(group = "Mixed", n = taxonomic_overlap)) %>%
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Mixed", "Invertebrate", "Vertebrate")))

panel_c <- ggplot(taxonomic_counts, aes(x = n, y = group, fill = group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = n),
    hjust = -0.35,
    size = base_size / .pt * 0.95,
    colour = colours["ink"]
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Vertebrate" = unname(colours["plum"]),
      "Invertebrate" = unname(colours["invertebrate"]),
      "Mixed" = unname(colours["slate"])
    ),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, n_syntheses + 5), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  labs(tag = "C", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_map() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank()
  )
```

## Panel E: Coverage breadth

```{r figure-1-systematic-map-evidence-matrix-6}
breadth_of <- function(long_data, variable, label) {
  long_data %>%
    count(study_id, name = "categories") %>%
    summarise(
      Multiple = sum(categories > 1),
      Single = sum(categories == 1),
      assignments = sum(categories)
    ) %>%
    mutate(dimension = label, mean_categories = assignments / n_syntheses)
}

breadth <- bind_rows(
  breadth_of(noise_long, noise_source, "Noise sources"),
  breadth_of(outcome_long, outcome_category, "Outcomes"),
  breadth_of(split_categories(map, ecosystem_type), ecosystem_type, "Environments"),
  breadth_of(taxonomic_membership, group, "Taxon groups")
) %>%
  mutate(dimension = fct_inorder(dimension) %>% fct_rev())

breadth_long <- breadth %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Multiple, Single), names_to = "breadth", values_to = "n") %>%
  mutate(breadth = factor(breadth, levels = c("Multiple", "Single")))

panel_e <- ggplot(breadth_long, aes(x = n, y = dimension, fill = breadth)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = n, colour = breadth),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
    size = base_size / .pt * 0.88
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Multiple" = unname(colours["breadth_multiple"]),
      "Single" = unname(colours["breadth_single"])
    ),
    labels = c("Multiple" = "Multiple categories", "Single" = "Single"),
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("Multiple" = "#FFFFFF", "Single" = unname(colours["muted_ink"])),
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, n_syntheses),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(ncol = 1)) +
  labs(tag = "E", x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_map() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.key.size = unit(11, "pt")
  )
```

## Assemble and save Figure 1

```{r figure-1-systematic-map-evidence-matrix-7}
panel_a <- panel_a + scale_y_continuous(breaks=c(0,5,10),
 limits=c(0,10.5),expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0))) + theme(
 axis.text.x=element_text(size=18,angle=45,hjust=1,vjust=1),
 axis.ticks.x=element_line(colour=colours["muted_ink"],linewidth=0.4),
 axis.ticks.length.x=unit(5,"pt"),
 axis.title.y=element_text(margin=margin(r=6)),
 plot.margin=margin(8,14,8,70),legend.key.size=unit(16,'pt'))
panel_b <- panel_b + theme(plot.margin=margin(10,42,4,12))
panel_c <- panel_c + theme(plot.margin=margin(32,18,18,12))
panel_d <- panel_d + theme(plot.margin=margin(10,18,18,12))
panel_e <- panel_e + theme(plot.margin=margin(10,18,4,12),legend.key.size=unit(16,'pt'))
right_column <- wrap_plots(panel_c,panel_d,panel_e,ncol=1,heights=c(.8,1,1.25))
# Explicit white gutter: labels from B cannot intrude into the right column.
body <- wrap_plots(wrap_elements(full=panel_b),plot_spacer(),wrap_elements(full=right_column),
 nrow=1,widths=c(10.1,.65,7.25))

panel_a <- panel_a + labs(tag=NULL)
panel_a_wrapper <- wrap_elements(full=panel_a) + labs(tag='A') +
 theme(plot.tag=figure1_panel_letter(),plot.tag.position=c(0.005,0.965),
       plot.margin=margin(0,0,0,0))
figure_1 <- wrap_plots(panel_a_wrapper,body,ncol=1,heights=c(3.65,8.35)) +
 plot_annotation(theme=theme(plot.margin=margin(10,10,10,10)))

# Wide layout, exported directly at 600 dpi when requested.
```

# Figure 2: Taxonomic groups

The treemap below is the reproducible, code-generated base of Figure 2.
The author's original animal illustrations and editable artwork are not distributed
with this repository. The submitted composition was assembled manually.

## Panel A: Taxonomic distribution TREEMAP
```{r figure-2-taxonomic-groups-1}
# Split and clean taxa
taxon_long4 <- map %>%
  separate_rows(scope_taxon, sep = ",") %>%
  mutate(
    scope_taxon = str_trim(scope_taxon),
    scope_taxon = str_to_title(scope_taxon)
  )

# Get unique study counts per taxon (no double-counting)
taxon_counts3 <- taxon_long4 %>%
  distinct(study_id, scope_taxon) %>%
  group_by(scope_taxon) %>%
  summarise(mentions = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Assign group and subgroup
 vertebrates <- c("Aves", "Mammalia", "Reptilia", "Fish", "Amphibia")

taxon_counts3 <- taxon_counts3 %>%
  mutate(
    group = if_else(scope_taxon %in% vertebrates, "Vertebrate", "Invertebrate"),
    subgroup = scope_taxon
  ) %>%
  filter(mentions > 0)

# Assign pastel green and pastel purple gradients
vertebrate_subgroups <- vertebrates
invertebrate_subgroups <- setdiff(unique(taxon_counts3$subgroup), vertebrates)

# Assign colours for each group: purple for vertebrates and green for invertebrates
pal_vertebrate <- scales::colour_ramp(c("#BBA0CA", "#600047"))(seq(0,1,length.out=length(vertebrate_subgroups)))
pal_invertebrate <- scales::colour_ramp(c("#B1B695", "#53917E"))(seq(0,1,length.out=length(invertebrate_subgroups)))

# Count data
taxon_counts3 <- taxon_counts3 %>%
  mutate(
    fill_color = case_when(
      group == "Vertebrate" ~ pal_vertebrate[match(subgroup, vertebrate_subgroups)],
      group == "Invertebrate" ~ pal_invertebrate[match(subgroup, invertebrate_subgroups)]
    ),
    label = paste0(scope_taxon, "\n(", mentions, ")")
  )

# Plot treemap (no subgroup label, just colored borders)
figure_2 <- ggplot(taxon_counts3, aes(area = mentions, fill = fill_color, label = label, subgroup = group)) +
  geom_treemap(color = "white", size = 1.8) +
  geom_treemap_subgroup_border(color = "white", size = 3) +   # Group borders only!
  # No geom_treemap_subgroup_text()  # <--- This removes the big faded group labels—for refining in vector editor software
  geom_treemap_text(
    fontface = "bold", colour = "White",
    place = "bottomleft", grow = FALSE, reflow = TRUE, min.size = 6
  ) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 20, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 13, hjust = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
  )

# Show figure
figure_2

# The submitted Figure 2 is a manual composition and is not overwritten.
if (isTRUE(params$export_figures)) {
  ggplot2::ggsave(here("Figures", "Final_figures", "Figure_2_taxonomic_scope_code_base.png"),
                 figure_2, width = 10, height = 7, dpi = 600, bg = "white")
```

# Figure 3: Bibliometric analysis

## Setup and country-name cleaning

```{r figure-3-bibliometric-analysis-1}
# Panel A uses the first author's first listed affiliation country.
# Panel B uses countries from ALL authors' affiliations, counted once per paper.
# Scopus separates authors with semicolons but concatenates an author's multiple
# affiliations with commas. The last country can therefore be a later affiliation.
# Match complete country tokens against this record's separate affiliation list,
# and return the first country in the first author's block (export order).
first_author_first_country <- function(authors_with_affiliations, affiliations) {
  stopifnot(length(authors_with_affiliations) == length(affiliations))
  normalise <- function(x) tolower(sub("\\.$", "", trimws(x)))

  vapply(seq_along(authors_with_affiliations), function(i) {
    if (is.na(authors_with_affiliations[i]) || is.na(affiliations[i])) {
      stop("Missing affiliation metadata at record ", i)
    }
    author_block <- strsplit(authors_with_affiliations[i], ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]][1]
    # The first two fields are the author's surname and given names.
    fields <- trimws(strsplit(author_block, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]])[-c(1, 2)]
    record_affiliations <- strsplit(affiliations[i], ";", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
    countries <- vapply(record_affiliations, function(x) {
      tail(trimws(strsplit(x, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]), 1)
    }, character(1))
    matches <- which(normalise(fields) %in% normalise(countries))
    if (!length(matches)) {
      stop("Cannot identify the first author's first affiliation country at record ", i)
    }
    fields[matches[1]]
  }, character(1))
}


# Direct Scopus and bibliometrix routes give the same international country pairs.
USE_BIBLIOMETRIX <- FALSE


colours <- c(
  ink = "#243746",
  muted_ink = "#52636F",
  paper = "white",
  land = "#E3E6E4",
  border = "#FBFAF8",
  graticule = "#DBE2E6"
)

base_size <- 16


# Constituent countries of the UK, plus the spellings Scopus emits.
uk_parts <- c("england", "scotland", "wales", "northern ireland", "uk",
              "united kingdom", "united kingdom.")

clean_country <- function(x) {
  x <- str_trim(x)
  x <- str_remove(x, "\\.$")
  low <- str_to_lower(str_trim(x))
  case_when(
    low %in% uk_parts ~ "United Kingdom",
    low %in% c("usa", "united states", "united states of america") ~ "United States",
    low == "russian federation" ~ "Russia",
    low == "czech republic" ~ "Czechia",
    low == "viet nam" ~ "Vietnam",
    TRUE ~ x
  )
}

# Country sits in the last comma-separated slot of a Scopus affiliation string.
country_of <- function(affiliation) {
  map_chr(affiliation, ~ {
    parts <- str_split(.x, ",")[[1]]
    clean_country(parts[length(parts)])
  })
}
```
## Panel A: First author’s first affiliation country

```{r figure-3-bibliometric-analysis-2}
first_author_records <- biblio %>%
  mutate(country = clean_country(first_author_first_country(
    authors_with_affiliations, affiliations
  )))

first_author_country <- first_author_records %>%
  count(country, name = "n_first_authors") %>%
  mutate(percent = 100 * n_first_authors / nrow(biblio)) %>%
  arrange(desc(n_first_authors), country)

# Include the largest count so the leading country is not censored by the scale.
map_count_max <- max(10, 2 * ceiling(max(first_author_country$n_first_authors) / 2))

n_records <- nrow(biblio)

world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") %>%
  filter(admin != "Antarctica")

# Natural Earth uses its own naming; align the few that differ from Scopus.
ne_lookup <- c(
  "United States of America" = "United States",
  "United Kingdom" = "United Kingdom",
  "Hong Kong S.A.R." = "Hong Kong"
)

world_first <- world %>%
  mutate(
    match_name = recode(admin, !!!ne_lookup)
  ) %>%
  left_join(first_author_country, by = c("match_name" = "country"))

# Fail explicitly if an affiliation country is missing from the map join.
stopifnot(
  sum(first_author_country$n_first_authors) == n_records,
  all(first_author_country$country %in% world_first$match_name)
)

first_author_country

# Equal Earth: equal-area, so country sizes are proportionally honest, and it
# keeps the rounded silhouette that reads better than a plate carree rectangle.
crs_equal_earth <- "EPSG:8857"

world_ee <- st_transform(world_first, crs_equal_earth)
graticule <- st_graticule(
  lat = seq(-60, 80, 20),
  lon = seq(-180, 180, 60)
) %>%
  st_transform(crs_equal_earth)

land_bbox <- st_bbox(world_ee)

fig3_panel_a <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = graticule, colour = colours["graticule"], linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(
    data = world_ee,
    aes(fill = n_first_authors),
    colour = colours["border"],
    linewidth = 0.12
  ) +
  scale_fill_stepsn(
    colours = c("#EBD9E6", "#D3A8CB", "#B173A8", "#8A4A82", "#5F2C5B"),
    na.value = colours["land"],
    breaks = seq(2, map_count_max, by = 2),
    limits = c(0, map_count_max),
    name = "First-author first-affiliation records",
    guide = guide_colorsteps(
      title.position = "top",
      barwidth = unit(190, "pt"),
      barheight = unit(10, "pt"),
      show.limits = FALSE
    )
  ) +
  # Crop to the land extent: with Antarctica dropped, the full projection would
  # leave a wide empty band of southern ocean.
  coord_sf(
    crs = crs_equal_earth,
    xlim = land_bbox[c("xmin", "xmax")],
    ylim = land_bbox[c("ymin", "ymax")],
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(tag = "A") +
  theme_void(base_size = base_size) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.margin = margin(t = 2, b = 2),
    legend.title = element_text(size = base_size - 0.5, colour = colours["muted_ink"]),
    legend.text = element_text(size = base_size - 1, colour = colours["muted_ink"]),
    plot.tag = main_panel_letter(),
    plot.tag.position = c(0.07, 0.92),
    plot.margin = margin(6, 6, 2, 6)
  )
```

## Panel B: Country co-authorship chord diagram

```{r figure-3-bibliometric-analysis-3}
# ALL authors’ affiliation countries, one row per record x country.
# Repeated authors/institutions in the same country do not multiply a paper’s weight.
record_countries <- biblio %>%
  mutate(record = row_number()) %>%
  select(record, affiliations) %>%
  separate_rows(affiliations, sep = ";") %>%
  filter(str_trim(affiliations) != "") %>%
  mutate(country = country_of(affiliations)) %>%
  distinct(record, country)

# Records per country drives which sectors are small enough to pool.
records_per_country <- count(record_countries, country, name = "n_records")

# --- Route 1: bibliometrix (the analysis used in Overview_figures.Rmd) --------
build_edges_bibliometrix <- function() {
  bib <- bibliometrix::convert2df(
    here("Data", "bibliometric.bib"),
    dbsource = "scopus",
    format = "bibtex"
  )
  bib <- bibliometrix::metaTagExtraction(bib, Field = "AU_CO", sep = ";")
  net <- bibliometrix::biblioNetwork(
    bib,
    analysis = "collaboration",
    network = "countries",
    sep = ";"
  )
  m <- as.matrix(net)
  diag(m) <- 0
  m[lower.tri(m)] <- 0
  # bibliometrix returns upper-case country names.
  dimnames(m) <- list(
    clean_country(str_to_title(rownames(m))),
    clean_country(str_to_title(colnames(m)))
  )
  as.data.frame(as.table(m)) %>%
    set_names(c("country.x", "country.y", "n")) %>%
    mutate(across(c(country.x, country.y), as.character)) %>%
    filter(n > 0, country.x != country.y)
}

# --- Route 2: direct from Scopus affiliation strings -------------------------
build_edges_direct <- function() {
  record_countries %>%
    inner_join(record_countries, by = "record", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    filter(country.x < country.y) %>%
    count(country.x, country.y, name = "n")
}

edges_raw <- if (USE_BIBLIOMETRIX) {
  build_edges_bibliometrix()
} else {
  build_edges_direct()
}

# Countries credited on a single record are pooled into one "Other" sector; the
# ring is otherwise dominated by hairline sectors carrying long labels.
other_countries <- records_per_country %>%
  filter(n_records == 1) %>%
  pull(country) %>%
  sort()

other_label <- paste0("Other (", length(other_countries), ")")

pool <- function(x) if_else(x %in% other_countries, other_label, x)

edges <- edges_raw %>%
  mutate(country.x = pool(country.x), country.y = pool(country.y)) %>%
  # Re-sort each pair alphabetically so pooled duplicates merge cleanly.
  mutate(
    a = pmin(country.x, country.y),
    b = pmax(country.x, country.y)
  ) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(n), .by = c(a, b)) %>%
  rename(country.x = a, country.y = b)

# Order sectors by total collaboration volume, with Other pinned to the end.
country_strength <- bind_rows(
  edges %>% select(country = country.x, n),
  edges %>% select(country = country.y, n)
) %>%
  summarise(strength = sum(n), .by = country) %>%
  arrange(country == other_label, desc(strength))

chord_order <- country_strength$country

# Shorter display labels keep the ring from being swamped by text.
display_label <- function(x) {
  recode(
    x,
    "United States" = "USA",
    "United Kingdom" = "UK",
    .default = x
  )
}

adjacency <- edges %>%
  rename(from = country.x, to = country.y) %>%
  filter(from %in% chord_order, to %in% chord_order)

# Palette: distinct hues for the high-volume sectors, muted for the long tail.
sector_colours <- setNames(
  colorRampPalette(
    c("#6C5FC7", "#91D3C5", "#5D5D5D", "#BCCF7F", "#A9C7E8", "#C49ACF",
      "#B28A85", "#7A8BD1", "#6BB6C9", "#D6A9A5", "#E8C1A8", "#9FBBB0")
  )(length(chord_order)),
  chord_order
)

draw_chord <- function() {
  circos.clear()
  circos.par(
    track.margin = c(0.005, 0.005),
    gap.degree = 2.2,
    start.degree = 90,
    points.overflow.warning = FALSE,
    # Room for the outer labels so long names are not clipped.
    canvas.xlim = c(-1.32, 1.32),
    canvas.ylim = c(-1.32, 1.32)
  )
  chordDiagram(
    adjacency,
    order = chord_order,
    grid.col = sector_colours,
    transparency = 0.28,
    annotationTrack = "grid",
    annotationTrackHeight = mm_h(4),
    preAllocateTracks = list(track.height = 0.17),
    directional = 0,
    link.sort = TRUE,
    link.decreasing = TRUE
  )
  circos.trackPlotRegion(
    track.index = 1,
    bg.border = NA,
    panel.fun = function(x, y) {
      xlim <- get.cell.meta.data("xlim")
      sector <- get.cell.meta.data("sector.index")
      # Keep radial labels just outside the coloured country sectors.
      circos.text(
        mean(xlim), 0.12, display_label(sector),
        facing = "clockwise",
        niceFacing = TRUE,
        adj = c(0, 0.5),
        cex = 1.65,
        col = "#243746"
      )
    }
  )
  circos.clear()
}

# Capture the base-graphics chord as a high-resolution raster grob. This keeps
# the ring circular in patchwork without an additional conversion package.
chord_png <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
grDevices::png(chord_png, width = 6000, height = 6000, res = 600, bg = "transparent")
draw_chord()
grDevices::dev.off()

chord_grob <- grid::rasterGrob(png::readPNG(chord_png), interpolate = TRUE)
unlink(chord_png)

fig3_panel_b <- patchwork::wrap_elements(full = chord_grob, clip = FALSE) +
  labs(tag = "B") +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "transparent", colour = NA),
    plot.tag = main_panel_letter(),
    plot.tag.position = c(0.07, 0.82),
    plot.margin = margin(-12, 6, 2, 6)
  )
```

```{r figure-4-policy-analysis-alluvial-plot-top-10-1}
# Call data

  select(policy_topic, ecological_context, policy_document_type)

# Count combinations

  group_by(policy_topic, ecological_context, policy_document_type) |>

# ---- Keep the top 10 most common combinations ----

dat_alluvial2 <- dat_alluvial |>
```

```{r figure-5-ceesat-scores-ceesat-question-scores-all-synth-1}
  # Prepare the 'value' column for plotting
  mutate(

    # Replace R's NA with a string "NA" for plotting
    value = ifelse(is.na(value), "NA", value),
```

# Syntheses quality analysis— Cited vs not cited in policy

```{r syntheses-quality-analysis-cited-vs-not-cited-in-policy-1, results="markup"}
# Match the manuscript's stated 64-point maximum for every synthesis.
dat <- dat_ceesat %>%
  filter(!is.na(raw_score)) %>%
  mutate(proportional_score = raw_score / 64)

# Confirm policy groups and check values
table(dat$cited_in_policy, useNA = "ifany")
summary(dat$proportional_score)
any(dat$proportional_score <= 0)

# Examine the distribution
hist(
  log(dat$proportional_score),
  main = "Log-transformed proportional CEESAT scores",
  xlab = "Log proportional score"
)

# Welch two-sample t-test
main_analysis <- t.test(
  log(proportional_score) ~ cited_in_policy,
  data = dat
)

main_analysis
```

# Figure S3: Synthesis characteristics and content mapping

```{r figure-s3-synthesis-characteristics-and-content-mapping-1}
# Recreate ComplexUpset's default styling with the installed ggplot2 version.
# ComplexUpset 1.3.3 bundles older theme objects that fail with ggplot2 4.x.
s3_upset_themes <- list(
  intersections_matrix = theme_minimal() + theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y = element_blank()
  ),
  "Intersection size" = theme_minimal() + theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank()
  ),
  overall_sizes = theme_minimal() + theme(
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
  ),
  default = theme_minimal() + theme(
    axis.text.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank()
  )
)
```

## Panel A: Review type by publication year

```{r figure-s3-synthesis-characteristics-and-content-mapping-2}
review_type_counts <- map %>%
  select(study_id, year, review_type) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  count(year, review_type, name = "paper_count") %>%
  complete(
    year = seq(min(map$year, na.rm = TRUE), max(map$year, na.rm = TRUE)),
    review_type = c("Systematic review", "Meta-analysis", "Systematic map"),
    fill = list(paper_count = 0)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    review_type = factor(
      review_type,
      levels = c("Systematic review", "Meta-analysis", "Systematic map")
    )
  )

figS3_a <- ggplot(
  review_type_counts,
  aes(x = year, y = paper_count, fill = review_type)
) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    data = filter(review_type_counts, paper_count > 0),
    aes(label = paper_count),
    position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = NULL,
    values = c(
      "Systematic review" = "#C6C1F0FF",
      "Meta-analysis" = "#F498B6FF",
      "Systematic map" = "#70C1BFFF"
    )
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(min(review_type_counts$year), max(review_type_counts$year), 1)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 12), breaks = seq(0, 12, 2)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of syntheses", tag = "A") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0.18, 0.78),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )
```

## Panel B: Environment average per paper

```{r figure-s3-synthesis-characteristics-and-content-mapping-3}
# Average number of environment types per paper
# sum(env_counts$paper_count)/50
# 1.56

# 1. Process ecosystem categories
env <- map %>%
  select(study_id, ecosystem_type) %>%
  mutate(ecosystem_type = str_split(ecosystem_type, ",\\s*")) %>%
  unnest(ecosystem_type) %>%
  mutate(ecosystem_type = str_trim(ecosystem_type)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ecosystem_type), ecosystem_type != "") %>%
  distinct(study_id, ecosystem_type)

# 2. Count syntheses per ecosystem category
env_counts <- env %>%
  count(ecosystem_type, name = "paper_count") %>%
  arrange(-paper_count) %>%
  mutate(ecosystem_type = fct_reorder(ecosystem_type, paper_count))

# 3. Calculate automatic label
n_syntheses <- n_distinct(map$study_id)
env_total_assignments <- sum(env_counts$paper_count)
env_mean_categories <- env_total_assignments / n_syntheses

env_label <- paste0(
  "Mean ecosystem categories per synthesis:\n",
  sprintf("%.2f", env_mean_categories),
  " (", env_total_assignments,
  " category assignments\nacross ",
  n_syntheses,
  " syntheses)"
)

# 4. Show summary statistics
env_counts %>%
  mutate(percentage = (paper_count / n_syntheses) * 100) %>%
  print(n = Inf)

# 5. UpSet plot data
dat_upset_env <- env |>
  mutate(value = 1) |>
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = study_id,
    names_from = ecosystem_type,
    values_from = value,
    values_fill = 0
  )

# 6. Plotting
figS3_b <- upset(
  dat_upset_env,
  themes = s3_upset_themes,
  stripes = upset_stripes(geom = geom_segment(linewidth = 7)),
  intersect = colnames(dat_upset_env)[-1],
  name = "",
  base_annotations = list(
    "Intersection size" = intersection_size(
      mapping = aes(fill = 'bars_color')
    ) +
      annotate(
        geom = "text", x = Inf, y = Inf,
        label = env_label,
        vjust = 1, hjust = 1
      ) +
      ylab("Number of syntheses") +
      scale_fill_manual(
        values = c('bars_color' = '#7370b3'),
        guide = 'none'
      ) +
      scale_y_continuous(
        limits = c(0, 20),
        breaks = seq(0, 20, 4)
      ) +
      labs(tag = "B") +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
      theme(
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x  = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank()
      )
  ),
  matrix = intersection_matrix(
    geom = geom_point(shape = 16, size = 1.8)
  ),
  set_sizes = FALSE,
  min_size = 0
)
```

```{r figure-s4-keywords-1}
dt.long

# Keyword synonym dictionary
synonyms <- c(

# ----Standardize case, trim whitespace ----
dt.long <- dt.long %>%
  mutate(value = str_to_title(value)) %>%
  mutate(value = trimws(value)) %>%
# Apply synonyms dictionary
  mutate(value = recode(value, !!!synonyms)) %>%
# drop NA
  filter(!is.na(value) & value != "")

# calculate number of mentions of each keyword—frequencies
keyword.freq <- dt.long %>%
  group_by(value) %>%
  summarize(n = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(n))

#-------Diagnostics-------
## number of mentions, including repeats
  nrow(dt.long)
## number of unique keywords after grouping
  nrow(keyword.freq)
## unique keyword count
  length(unique(dt.long$value))

## Find missing data
#setdiff(unique(dt.long$value), keyword.freq$value)

keyword.freq <- keyword.freq %>%
  arrange(-n)

# Clean NA
keyword.freq_clean <- keyword.freq %>%
  filter(!is.na(value))

# Reorder factor levels based on frequency for plotting
keyword.freq$value <- factor(keyword.freq$value,
                             levels = rev(keyword.freq$value))

# Plot
figS4_a <- ggplot(data = keyword.freq[1:20, ],
                    aes(x = n, y = value, fill = n))+
  geom_col()+
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#B4D8E4", high = "#00425E")+
  xlab("Number of keywords")+
  ylab("Keyword")+
  #theme_bw()
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
      theme(
        panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),   # remove x axis title
        #axis.text.y  = element_blank(),   # remove x axis text
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank()
      )

#Save
```

## Assemble Figure S4

The code embeds the publication word-cloud raster and its exact frequency input.
If the keywords change, replace the embedded raster and frequency table before
assembling S4; the check prevents a stale cloud being used.

```{r embedded-cloud-asset, include=FALSE}
# Frozen publication word cloud and its source frequencies, embedded for portability.
cloud_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
cloud_counts_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeBin(base64enc::base64decode(""), cloud_file)
writeBin(base64enc::base64decode(""), cloud_counts_file)
```

```{r figure-s4-assemble}
if (!file.exists(cloud_file) || !file.exists(cloud_counts_file)) {
  stop("Export figS4_b and its keyword.freq table before assembling Figure S4.")
}
cloud_counts <- read_csv(cloud_counts_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
current_counts <- keyword.freq %>% mutate(value = as.character(value))
if (!isTRUE(all.equal(as.data.frame(cloud_counts), as.data.frame(current_counts)))) {
  stop("S4 word-cloud frequencies changed. Re-export figS4_b and its frequency CSV.")
}
cloud_panel <- patchwork::wrap_elements(full = grid::rasterGrob(
  png::readPNG(cloud_file), interpolate = FALSE
))
figS4 <- (figS4_a / cloud_panel) +
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1)) + plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") &
  theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10))
save_supplementary_figure(here("Figures", "Supplementary", "Figure_S4_keywords.png"), figS4,
       width = 8, height = 10.35, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
save_supplementary_figure(here("Figures", "Supplementary", "Figure_S4_keywords.pdf"), figS4,
       width = 8, height = 10.35, bg = "white")
figS4
unlink(c(cloud_file, cloud_counts_file))
```


# Figure S5: Academic citation count and the three most cited syntheses
```{r figure-s5-academic-citation-count-and-the-three-most-ci-1}
# 1. Create empty label column
biblio$label <- NA

# 2. Assign labels to the three top-cited papers
biblio$label[grepl("Benítez-López", biblio$authors) & biblio$year == 2010] <- "Benítez-López et al., 2010"
biblio$label[grepl("Shannon",       biblio$authors) & biblio$year == 2016] <- "Shannon et al., 2016"
biblio$label[grepl("Duarte",        biblio$authors) & biblio$year == 2021] <- "Duarte et al., 2021"

# Draw each study once. Only unlabelled studies are jittered; highlighted
# points and their labels share the exact publication year and citation count.
figS5 <- ggplot(biblio, aes(x = year, y = cited_by)) +
  geom_point(data = subset(biblio, is.na(label)),
             position = position_jitter(width = 0.3, height = 0, seed = 20261009),
             size = 3.3, alpha = 0.35, color = "#8074A8FF") +
  geom_point(data = subset(biblio, !is.na(label)),
             aes(x = year, y = cited_by),
             color = "#8074A8FF", size = 4.3) +
  geom_label(data = subset(biblio, !is.na(label)),
             # Place the rightmost highlighted study's label to its left.
             aes(label = label,
                 x = year + if_else(grepl("^Duarte", label), -0.35, 0.35),
                 hjust = if_else(grepl("^Duarte", label), 1, 0)),
             vjust = 0.5, size = 10.5 / .pt,
             label.padding = unit(0.15, "lines"), linewidth = 0.25,
             fill = "white", color = "black"
  ) +
   labs(
     x = NULL,
    y = "Academic citation count"#,
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(from = min(biblio$year),
                                  to = max(biblio$year), by = 1),
                     expand = expansion(add = c(0.6, 1.2))
                     )+
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 9, colour = "#333333"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9, colour = "#333333"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 11, margin = margin(r = 12)),
    axis.line.x = element_line(colour = "#666666", linewidth = 0.35),
    axis.ticks.x = element_line(colour = "#666666", linewidth = 0.35),
    axis.ticks.length.x = unit(3, "pt"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(12, 18, 12, 12)

  )


# 4. Print plot
figS5
```

# Figure S6: Policy analysis, alluvial plot all variables

```{r figure-s6-policy-analysis-alluvial-plot-all-variables-1}
# Alluvial plot with shared Figure 4 colours by document type ----
dat <- dat_policy |>
  select(policy_topic, ecological_context, policy_document_type)

dat_alluvial <- dat |>
  group_by(policy_topic, ecological_context, policy_document_type) |>
  summarise(Freq = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Prefix axis labels for uniqueness and reorder by frequency
dat_alluvial2 <- dat_alluvial |>
  mutate(
    policy_topic        = fct_reorder(as.factor(policy_topic), Freq, .fun = sum, .desc = TRUE),
    ecological_context  = fct_reorder(as.factor(ecological_context), Freq, .fun = sum, .desc = TRUE),
    policy_document_type = fct_reorder(as.factor(policy_document_type), Freq, .fun = sum, .desc = TRUE)
  ) |>
  # 🔑 Wrap long labels in Document type only
  mutate(
    policy_document_type = fct_relabel(policy_document_type, ~ str_replace_all(.x,
                                                                      c("Government policy"        = "Government\npolicy",
                                                                        "Regulatory Submission"    = "Regulatory\nSubmission",
                                                                        "Intergovernmental policy" = "Intergovernmental\npolicy")))
  )


# Match Figure 4 for the shared document types; retain the additional category colours.
unicorn_pastel <- c(
  "Government\npolicy"        = "#B393BA",
  "Regulatory\nSubmission"    = "#91B6AA",
  "Intergovernmental\npolicy" = "#CEA0A5",
  "NGO report"                = "#B7D9EB",
  "Think Tank"                = "#D6D6F8",
  "Academic advisory"        = "#FFE3A3",
  "Other document"           = "#B6E06E"
)

# ---- Plot ----
figS6 <- ggplot(dat_alluvial2,
                       aes(axis1 = policy_document_type,
                           axis2 = ecological_context,
                           axis3 = policy_topic,
                           y = Freq)
) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("policy_document_type", "ecological_context", "policy_topic"),
    labels = c("Document type", "Ecological context", "Policy topic"),
    position = "top",
    expand = c(.12, .12)
  ) +
 # Match ribbon and column widths so every attachment is visible.
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = policy_document_type),
                width = 1/3, alpha = 0.8, knot.pos = 0.4,
                colour = "white", linewidth = 1/35) +
  geom_stratum(aes(fill = after_stat(stratum)),
               color = "white", linewidth = 1.2, width = 1/3) +
  geom_text(stat = "stratum",
            aes(label = ifelse(after_stat(count) >= 18, as.character(after_stat(stratum)), "")),
            size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = unicorn_pastel, na.value = "#E8E9EB") +
  # Keep the column headings close to the tops of the strata.
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.10, 0))) +

  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  labs(y = "Count of papers", x = NULL) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y  = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x.top = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, margin = margin(b = 2)),
    axis.ticks.length.x.top = unit(0, "pt"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.border = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )


# Move labels for very small strata into the bottom margin, with leader lines.
# These are annotations only: the ribbon and stratum heights remain unchanged.
s6_strata <- ggplot_build(figS6)$data[[2]]
s6_small_labels <- s6_strata |>
  filter(count < 18) |>
  group_by(x) |>
  arrange(desc(y), .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(label_y = -10 - 14 * (row_number() - 1)) |>
  ungroup()
figS6 <- figS6 +
  geom_segment(data = s6_small_labels,
               aes(x = x + 1/6, xend = x + 0.23, y = y, yend = label_y),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#52636F", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_segment(data = s6_small_labels,
               aes(x = x + 0.23, xend = x + nchar(as.character(stratum)) * 0.006 + 0.02, y = label_y, yend = label_y),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "#52636F", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_text(data = s6_small_labels,
            aes(x = x, y = label_y, label = stratum),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.1)
figS6
save_supplementary_figure(here("Figures", "Supplementary", "Figure_S6_alluvialplot.pdf"), figS6, width = 10, height = 10, bg = "white")
save_supplementary_figure(here("Figures", "Supplementary", "Figure_S6_alluvialplot.png"), figS6, width = 10, height = 10, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

# Figure S8: Policy trends

Count the retained policy citation records in Dataset3 by policy publication year.
Each source row contributes once per panel, including repeated entries retained
by the researcher because they may represent chapter or compilation citations.
These are citation-record counts; the table does not establish unique documents.

# Figure S9: Annual trends in syntheses cited and not cited in policy

```{r figure-s9-annual-trends-in-syntheses-cited-and-not-cite-1}
# Tidy data
tidy_trends <- map %>%
  select(study_id, year, cited_policy, outcome_category, noise_source, ecosystem_type) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(outcome_category, noise_source, ecosystem_type),
    names_to = "category_group",
    values_to = "category_value"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(category_value), category_value != "") %>%
  separate_rows(category_value, sep = "[,;]\\s*") %>%
  mutate(category_value = str_trim(category_value)) %>%

# Filter out "NA" values as requested
  filter(category_value != "NA") %>%
 # Selecting columns to plot
  group_by(year, cited_policy, category_group, category_value) %>%
  summarise(n = n_distinct(study_id), .groups = "drop")

# Creating a plotting function
create_trend_plot <- function(df, legend_title, plot_title = NULL) {

  ggplot(df, aes(x = year, y = n, fill = category_value)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.8, position = position_stack()) +

    # Count for each segment inside the bar
    geom_text(
      aes(label = n),
      position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5),
      size = 5,
      colour = "white",
      fontface = "bold"
    ) +

    scale_fill_paletteer_d("ggthemes::Purple_Pink_Gray", name = legend_title) +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = seq(2008, 2025, 1),
      # Include the full width of the first and last bars (width = 0.8).
      limits = c(2007.5, 2025.5)
    ) +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, 30),
      breaks = seq(0, 30, 5)
  )+
    labs(
      title = plot_title, # Title will be applied only if provided
      x = NULL,
      y = "Number of syntheses"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 16),
      legend.title = element_blank (),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5), # Larger title
      legend.position ="inside", legend.position.inside = c(.15, .65),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 18),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 18),
      axis.title.x = element_text(size = 18)
    )
}
```

# Figure S10: Geographical distribution of policy citation records

Count all retained citation records using their coded publication location.
The derived plotting table maps Nairobi to Kenya and combines UK constituent
labels; the source data and the international scope of the UNEP report remain
unchanged. European Union, International and Mixed records are reported separately
and are not redistributed to country polygons.

## Panel A: Publication countries
```{r figure-s10-geographical-distribution-of-policy-1}
policy_location_data <- dat_policy %>%
  mutate(policy_country_clean = case_when(
    str_trim(policy_country) %in% c("Northern Ireland", "Scotland", "United Kingdom") ~ "United Kingdom",
    str_trim(policy_country) %in% c("USA", "U.S.A.", "United States") ~ "United States of America",
    # UNEP's GEO-6 publication location is Nairobi, Kenya (Dataset3 row 290).
    str_trim(policy_country) == "Nairobi" ~ "Kenya",
    TRUE ~ str_trim(policy_country)
  ))
stopifnot(!anyNA(policy_location_data$policy_country_clean),
          all(nzchar(policy_location_data$policy_country_clean)))
policy_counts <- policy_location_data %>%
  count(policy_country_clean, name = "n", sort = TRUE)
non_country_labels <- c("International", "European Union", "Mixed")
non_country_counts <- policy_counts %>%
  filter(policy_country_clean %in% non_country_labels)
country_specific_counts <- policy_counts %>%
  filter(!policy_country_clean %in% non_country_labels)

world <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
unmatched_countries <- country_specific_counts %>%
  anti_join(sf::st_drop_geometry(world), by = c("policy_country_clean" = "name"))
if (nrow(unmatched_countries)) {
  stop("Unmatched S10 publication countries: ",
       paste(unmatched_countries$policy_country_clean, collapse = ", "))
}
stopifnot(sum(country_specific_counts$n) + sum(non_country_counts$n) == nrow(dat_policy))
map_data <- world %>%
  left_join(country_specific_counts, by = c("name" = "policy_country_clean"))
non_country_note <- non_country_counts %>%
  arrange(match(policy_country_clean, non_country_labels)) %>%
  transmute(label = paste0(policy_country_clean, " (", n, ")")) %>%
  pull(label) %>% paste(collapse = "; ")

figS10_a <- ggplot(map_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = n), colour = NA) +
  coord_sf(ylim = c(-60, 85), expand = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_paletteer_c("ggthemes::Purple", na.value = "#D8D8D8FF",
                        labels = number_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(fill = "Policy citation records",
       caption = paste0("Not assigned to country polygons: ", non_country_note,
                        ".\nGrey: no country-attributed records in Dataset S3.")) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 9, margin = margin(t = 5))) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", barwidth = 15, barheight = 0.5))
# Intermediate panel: figS10_a
```

## Panel A: CEESAT scores (syntheses cited in policy):

```{r figure-s11-ceesat-scores-cited-and-not-cited-in-policy-1}
# 1. Labels
labels <- structure(list(q = c("1.1", "2.1", "3.1", "3.2", "4.1", "4.2",
"4.3", "5.1", "5.2", "6.1", "6.2", "6.3", "7.1", "7.2", "7.3",
"8.1"), label = c("1.1 Research question and criteria",
"2.1 A priori protocol", "3.1 Systematic search approach",

"6.1 Data extraction method", "6.2 Data availability",
"6.3 Data extraction cross-check",
"7.1 Choice of synthesis approach", "7.2 Appropriate meta-analysis",
"7.3 Variability investigation",
"8.1 Synthesis limitations"
)), row.names = c(NA, -16L), class = c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame"
))


# 2. Prepare the data for BOTH plots
# Data for CITED plot
ceesat_cited_for_plot <- dat_ceesat %>%
  filter(cited_in_policy == 1) %>%
  select(starts_with("CEESAT")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(CEESAT7.2, CEESAT7.3), ~suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(item, value) %>% summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(item) %>% mutate(percent = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  mutate(q = str_remove(item, "CEESAT")) %>%
  left_join(labels, by = "q") %>%
  mutate(
    value = as.character(value),
    value = ifelse(is.na(value), "NA", value),
    value = factor(value, levels = c("4", "3", "1", "0", "NA"))
  )

# Data for NOT CITED plot
ceesat_not_cited_for_plot <- dat_ceesat %>%
  filter(cited_in_policy == 0) %>%
  select(starts_with("CEESAT")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(CEESAT7.2, CEESAT7.3), ~suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(item, value) %>% summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(item) %>% mutate(percent = n / sum(n) * 100) %>%
  mutate(q = str_remove(item, "CEESAT")) %>%
  left_join(labels, by = "q") %>%
  mutate(
    value = as.character(value),
    value = ifelse(is.na(value), "NA", value),
    value = factor(value, levels = c("4", "3", "1", "0", "NA"))
  )


# 3. Create the individual plots with updated themes
common_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14) # Increase percentage label size for both plots
  )

# Plot A: Cited
figS11_a <- ggplot(ceesat_cited_for_plot, aes(x = fct_rev(label), y = percent, fill = value)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 5, color = "black") +

# Plot B: Not Cited
```

# Reproducibility checks

```{r validate-analysis, include=FALSE}
stopifnot(nrow(map) == 50L, nrow(biblio) == 47L,
          nrow(dat_policy) == 537L, nrow(dat_ceesat) == 50L,
          sum(country_specific_counts$n) == 447L,
          sum(non_country_counts$n) == 90L)
validate_alluvial <- function(plot, total, combinations) {
  layers <- ggplot2::ggplot_build(plot)$data
  flows <- layers[[1]]
  strata <- layers[[2]]
  stopifnot(length(unique(flows$alluvium)) == combinations)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(flows))) {
    f <- flows[i, ]
    s <- strata[strata$x == f$x & strata$stratum == f$stratum, ]
    stopifnot(nrow(s) == 1L, f$ymin >= s$ymin - 1e-8,
              f$ymax <= s$ymax + 1e-8)
  }
  stopifnot(all(tapply(flows$ymax - flows$ymin, flows$x, sum) == total))
}
validate_alluvial(figure_4, 327, 10)
validate_alluvial(figS6, 537, 85)
```

```{=html}
<script>

// Arrange the freshly rendered report; no figures or results are recomputed here.
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
  const sourceSections = [...document.querySelectorAll('div.section.level1')];
  const template = document.getElementById('research-companion-layout');
  if (!template || !sourceSections.length) return;
  const layout = template.content.cloneNode(true);
  for (const source of sourceSections) {
    const article = document.createElement('article');
    article.id = source.id;
    article.className = 'figure-section';
    const title = source.querySelector('h1').textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim();
    const heading = document.createElement('h3');
    heading.textContent = title;
    article.append(heading);
    const notes = source.cloneNode(true);
    notes.querySelector('h1').remove();
    if (source.id === 'figure-2-taxonomic-groups') {
      const note = document.createElement('p');
      note.className = 'small';
      note.textContent = 'Code-generated plot base; the author’s original animal artwork is not included in this report.';
      article.append(note);
    }
    for (const img of [...notes.querySelectorAll('img')]) {
      const container = document.createElement('div');
      container.className = 'figure';
      const localHeading = img.closest('.section')?.querySelector('h2');
      img.alt = localHeading ? localHeading.textContent.trim() : title;
      img.removeAttribute('width');
      img.removeAttribute('height');
      img.style.width = 'auto';
      img.loading = 'lazy';
      container.append(img);
      article.append(container);
    }
    const details = document.createElement('details');
    details.className = 'code';
    const summary = document.createElement('summary');
    summary.textContent = 'View code and analysis notes';
    const codeBody = document.createElement('div');
    codeBody.className = 'code-body';
    codeBody.append(...notes.childNodes);
    details.append(summary, codeBody);
    article.append(details);
    const target = /^figure-[1-5]-/.test(source.id) ? '#main-figures'
      : (source.id === 'supplementary-figures' || source.id.startsWith('figure-s'))
        ? '#supplement' : '#analysis';
    layout.querySelector(target).append(article);
  }
  document.body.replaceChildren(layout);
  const links = [...document.querySelectorAll('aside nav a')];
  const sections = links.map(a => document.querySelector(a.getAttribute('href')));
  function markActiveSection() {
    let current = sections[0];
    for (const section of sections) if (section.getBoundingClientRect().top < 180) current = section;
    for (const link of links) link.classList.toggle('active', link.hash === '#' + current.id);
  }
  window.addEventListener('scroll', markActiveSection, {passive: true});
  markActiveSection();
  if (location.hash) document.getElementById(decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1)))?.scrollIntoView();
});
</script>
```
